points: Yirmiyahu tells the people of Binyamin, who fled to Yerushalayim for safety, to leave. Throughout history we run to a "safe" place, like Portugal after Spain or Hungary in the war, and it isn't safe.
The Malbim: Tzion is like a pampered girl asleep while the city falls. The people were so overwhelmed they gave up instead of fighting.
Yirmiyahu is frustrated: their ears are blocked, no one listens. Hashem tells him to keep speaking. As Rav Kook said, "I write not because I have the strength, but because I can't stay silent."
"Gam bosh lo yeivoshu": sin is human, but as long as we feel some shame there's hope. Boasting about it is when all is lost.
The Malbim on the metals that aren't silver: each group, Chassidish, Modern Orthodox, Yeshivish, points at the other's flaws. Every group is imperfect; look in the mirror instead.
